# Callsign

> Generate codenames for projects and services in the grammar of Armored Core VI manufacturers: a 3-letter acronym for each project, a weapon name for each tool, and a whole system named as one build.

- Live: https://callsign.neorgon.com/
- Part of the Neorgon tool suite (free, no signup, runs in your browser): https://neorgon.com/
- Keywords: codename generator, project names, service names, repo names, acronyms, naming convention, Armored Core, AC6
- Unofficial fan tool, not affiliated with FromSoftware or Bandai Namco Entertainment.

## What it does

A plate is a pure function of four inputs: the words that describe the thing, a house (one manufacturer's naming grammar), a slot (where the thing sits in a build) and a roll number. The same four inputs give the same plate for as long as the grammar version stays the same. A plate carries a designation such as `IB-C03B: RAD 386`, a callsign (the acronym for a part, the name for a weapon), 3-letter and 4-letter acronyms, and a reading of what the letters stand for.

Part slots name a project or a platform piece and answer to an acronym: `head` (frontend), `core` (main service), `arms` (integrations), `legs` (infrastructure), `booster` (CI/CD), `fcs` (monitoring), `generator` (data store), `expansion` (failover).

Weapon slots name one tool or service each and answer to a name: `rifle`, `machinegun`, `gatling`, `shotgun`, `handgun`, `linear`, `sniper`, `bazooka`, `grenade`, `missile`, `flamer`, `laser`, `plasma`, `drone`, `blade`, `pilebunker`, `stun`, `shield`.

House ids for the game's own manufacturers: `balam` `dafeng` `arquebus` `add` `schneider` `furlong` `vcpl` `melinite` `takigawa` `baws` `elcano` `rad` `allmind` `ibis` `ia`. Callsign's own houses, not in the game, in the same style: `apojove` (outer-system moons), `umklapp` (exotic particles), `vastitas` (megastructures and drives), `quadnil` (placeholder element names), `peristome` (strange flora), `siboga` (deep sea and extremophiles), `protyle` (retired constellations and spent science). `ibis` stamps the acronym of your own words into its designation, and `allmind` stamps your longest word into its weapon names: vowels dropped, cut to four letters, when at least three are left.

## Deep links: open a name in someone's browser

Build a link instead of describing a name by hand.

- One plate: `https://callsign.neorgon.com/?via=agent&s=<words>&h=<house id|all>&p=<slot id>&r=<roll>&g=1#forge`
  - `s` is the description, URL-encoded, up to 120 characters; the page reads only the first 120 and says so. Three or four capital letters on their own (`RAD`) are taken as the acronym itself; `rad` in lowercase is a word.
  - With one house the page shows six plates from roll `r` on, and the first is the plate the link names. With `h=all` it shows one plate per house at roll `r`.
  - `r` is a whole number from 0 to 999999; leave it out for 0. Anything else opens roll 0 with a notice.
- A whole build: `https://callsign.neorgon.com/?via=agent&b=<payload>&g=1#garage`. The payload is the garage JSON as base64url over its UTF-8 bytes with the padding stripped (Node: `Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(garage), 'utf8').toString('base64url')`). The garage shape is whatever the page's own share link carries (an object with `parts` and `weapons` arrays); decode one to see it. Keep the whole URL under 8,000 characters: GitHub Pages refuses longer ones. Opening a build link replaces the visitor's working build, so the page first keeps theirs in the hangar.
- `g` is the grammar version. A link whose `g` differs from the page's grammar opens with a notice, because its names may have changed. A link that carries `s`, `h`, `p`, `r` or `b` but no `g` was made before grammars were numbered and counts as grammar 0. An unknown house or slot id falls back to every house and to `core`, and the page says so.
- Add `via=<name>` to say who sent the visitor; it is counted, never shown. Agents and skills use `via=agent`. It belongs in the query, before the `#`.
- When a name must never change, store the designation text, not the link.
- Word families: `https://callsign.neorgon.com/?via=agent&fam=<family id>&g=1#lexicon` shows one family on its own, with its sources and the houses that use it; a family of more than 24 words opens as a preview of 8 words per list, with a Show all button. `sub=<subject id>` and `lang=<language id>` filter the list instead (a `fam` in the same link wins and the filters reset), and `find=<a word or a designation>` looks one up; a lookup that is or holds a real in-game designation is refused without echoing it. Family ids: `entomologists` `chinese-asterisms` `german-birds` `melinite-words` `basho-school` `spanish-words` `rad-phrases` `allmind-words` `institute-words` `outer-moons` `exotic-particles` `megastructures` `placeholder-elements` `strange-flora` `deep-sea-extremophiles` `spent-science`. Subject ids: `space` `physics` `chemistry` `engineering` `animals` `plants` `microbes` `anatomy` `myth` `people` `mind` `weather` `history` `everyday`. Language ids: `en` `de` `es` `zh` `ja` `la` `el` `non` `many`. An unknown id shows every family and says so.

## Command line and skill

In a checkout of https://github.com/energon-a-secas/callsign-site, with Node 22 LTS or later, `node tools/callsign.mjs forge "billing dashboard" --house balam --slot head --json` prints the same plates as the page, with no network. `houses`, `slots` and `families` list the ids, `lookup <word or designation>` says which house and word family a name comes from, `identity`, `garage` and `link` cover the rest, and exit code 2 means an unknown id or option. It cuts a description to the 120 characters a link carries, so the plate it prints is the plate its link opens. The neorgon-forge Claude Code plugin ships a `callsign` skill that runs this tool.

## Terms

The house grammars are patterns read off the game's part names, not statements from its developers. Callsign's word pools are its own picks from public sources, and it does not republish the game's part catalogue: do not present real in-game part names as Callsign output.
